groups.why: Both rows check the same thing on the column/measure setting popup: pressing Save/OK with no changes must not trigger a re-query.
All four rows check the same expectation: the measure setting order is saved and query-result measures appear in that saved order.
Both rows cover a user with no saved personalization switching Div, where columns and measures must use that Div's UI Category Default.
This is a separate screen rule (EG395, Column button after save), so it stays alone.
This row mixes four expectations into one, so it does not match any single other row and stays alone.
This checks something no other row covers: re-querying setting candidates by the auto-selected Division before Search.
Its condition is the Div 40→81→40 switch, unlike V-db407b00, and that row's expected result has an extra item (selected columns must appear in results), so they stay apart.
Besides the required-column restriction, it also expects user-selected columns to always appear in query results, so its expected result differs.
This checks only that the Measure Setting button is removed (shown 0 times), which no other row covers.
This targets different elements (the VERSION and AS FROM SITE columns) from every other row.
This checks staying on the new tab after save and the Default basis after a save→Close→reopen sequence, a different state and expectation from the Default button restore in V-fd5f67d5.
This checks the MKT FCST[R+P] measure name, a different element.
This checks that required columns are kept and added back on a Div switch after saving personalization, a different state from the other rows.
This checks which measures are added or removed for each Div, a different element and expectation.
This checks that the query grid is built from the column settings and hides internal columns, a different expectation.
This checks that the grid is rebuilt right away when column settings OK is pressed, which differs from the no-change, no-re-query rows.
This combines a row count, Team Name display, and the saved column layout for one specific period, so it differs from every other row.
This checks only that clicking the Column Setting popup's Default button restores the base column layout, so it stays alone.
